newsitem.title: NORWAY: North Sea oil/NGL Feb output 6.17 mln bpd - analysts.
newsitem.headline: North Sea oil/NGL Feb output 6.17 mln bpd - analysts.

text.p: North Sea oil and natural gas liquids (NGL) output amounted to 6.17 million barrels per day (bpd) in February, a slip of 50,000 bpd from January's average, according to industry analysts Wood Mackenzie.
Britain pumped 2.51 million bpd, excluding just over 100,000 bpd of onshore production, down from 2.56 million bpd in January, Wood Mackenzie said in its latest monthly report.

Norwegian oil/NGL production was up 10,000 bpd at 3.40 million bpd despite disruptions to offshore loadings at the Statfjord and Gullfaks developments, which led to several shutdowns at some platforms.

Closures at Gullfaks resulted in a fall of around 45,000 bpd at the field to 428,000 bpd and a decrease of about 13,000 bpd at Tordis, which feeds crude to Gullfaks for processing and loading, to 76,000 bpd.

Production was also halted at Saga Petroleum's Snorre platform, which resulted in a 40,000 bpd drop in average throughput to 200,000 bpd. Snorre pumps oil to Statfjord for loading into shuttle tankers.

Gains in production in February were noted at Phillip's Ekofisk field following pipeline problems in January, Statoil's Heidrun and Norsk Hydro's Troll, which reached its highest level yet at around 262,000 bpd, the analysts said.

In the Danish sector output fell around five percent, or 11,000 bpd, to average 217,000 bpd. Wood Mackenzie attributed the slip largely to a drop of around 3,000 bpd from Grom and 8,000 bpd from Svend.
Dutch oil/NGL production fell by seven percent or around 2,500 bpd to 34,000 bpd in February due to small decreases in output at most fields, Wood Mackenzie said.
